findings.title: Public method `findMany` removed without replacement, breaking existing callers
findings.body: The previous public API method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` has been removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()` which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing callers of `findMany` in the codebase will fail at compile time. Since only two files are changed in this PR, callers elsewhere are not updated. This is a breaking API change that requires coordinated updates or a deprecation path.

findings.title: Dead code branches in `getBaseConditions` — `authConditions` is always truthy
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` has return type `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null or undefined). Therefore the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the `else` branch (line 78) in `getBaseConditions` are unreachable dead code. While the function still produces correct results, the misleading control flow may confuse future maintainers into thinking `authConditions` can be falsy, and the `NOTHING_CONDITION` fallback on line 79 can never be reached from this path.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous test suite included a 'Caching' describe block that verified `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on repeated calls. These tests were removed in this PR, but the caching logic (using `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` fields) still exists in the service. There is now no test coverage for this behavior, meaning a regression that breaks caching (e.g., accidentally removing the cache check) would go undetected.

findings.title: Integration test assumes exact result set from a denormalized view without controlling all data
findings.body: The `getBaseConditions` test at line 481 queries `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` with `WHERE ${baseConditions}` and asserts the result is exactly `[{ id: userBooking.id }]`. If other tests running in parallel (or leftover data from failed tests) create bookings matching the same user-scope condition (`userId = X AND teamId IS NULL`), this assertion will fail non-deterministically. The test creates its own user but does not isolate against concurrent test data that might reference the same user or match the condition.
